key_insight: Transient XUV spectroscopy reveals ultrafast hole transfer from Re to Se and signatures of electron localization in Re₆Se₈Cl₂ superatomic crystals, linking charge redistribution to phonon motion.
engineering_relevance: Element-resolved carrier dynamics offer a basis for tuning charge transport and electron–phonon coupling in superatomic optoelectronic materials.
method: Simultaneously probe the Re O₂ and Se M₄,₅ edges using transient XUV spectroscopy.
Correlate spectral features to distinguish electron, hole, band-gap, and phonon dynamics.
evidence_signal: Correlated Re and Se transient spectra support inferred flat conduction bands, hot-hole transfer from Re to Se, and phonon oscillations driven by hole-mediated displacive excitation.
watch_item: The abstract reports spectroscopic inferences rather than device-level transport measurements or demonstrated optoelectronic performance.
paper_title: Ultrafast Hole Transport and Electron Localization in Superatomic Re$_{6}$Se$_{8}$Cl$_{2}$
